A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMDiT probing and enhancement work, despite the title change to TexTailor. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable throughout both PDFs. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes supplementary Sections A–G.

before.justification: v1 reports original block-intervention experiments, generation benchmarks, editing evaluations, acceleration measurements, and ablations across SD3.5, FLUX, and Qwen Image.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds robustness experiments, unseen-attribute evaluations, token-level comparisons, failure cases, and generation human-preference results.

M1.justification: The enhancement formula is retained, but block selection changes substantially. v1 Table 1 specifies attribute-specific sets, whereas v2 Table 1 uses one shared set per model for all attributes. For example, FLUX counting moves from blocks {32,37,45,49,54} to {2,7,12,17,22}, changing which internal representations receive enhancement.

E1.justification: The main quantitative probing dataset changes from GPT-5-generated color/amount/spatial prompts to HPDv2/COCO-derived color/shape/spatial prompts. Appendix E.6 additionally evaluates unseen Lighting and Art Style attributes. The three model families and main generation, editing, and acceleration tasks remain; Appendix D.2 confirms that the shortened CompBench name still denotes CompBench++ coverage.

E2.justification: TACA, including its two FLUX configurations, remains the generation comparator; Stable Flow remains the editing comparator; FLUX and TeaCache remain the acceleration baselines. Added scaling and CFG-skipping configurations expand analyses of the proposed approach. Newly discussed Semantic Routing and HyperAlign are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The probing sample increases from 333 to 633 prompts, and shape evaluation with Qwen-VL replaces the quantitative CountGD-based amount probe. New experiments vary samplers, denoising steps, resolution, and CFG. Appendix G reports three editing participants, whereas v1 reports twelve; this is a reported protocol revision, although the retained vote totals leave the executed human-study design unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation with sampler/step/resolution robustness, CFG controls, unseen-attribute transfer, varying enhancement schedules, token-versus-sentence comparisons, and illustrated failure cases. Existing scale and block-selection ablations are retained and extended with additional models and attributes in Appendix E.

E5.justification: The numerical ± summaries accompanying generation-quality, editing, and acceleration scores in v1 disappear from the corresponding v2 tables and are not restored in the appendix. The redrawn probing plots also omit v1's shaded variability bands. Five-seed probing remains; Appendix C.1 newly identifies the seeds and explicitly describes averaging, without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for revised probing, token-level color/shape enhancement, sentence-level counting, robustness, acceleration variants, and human preferences. Table E.7 newly reports Lighting accuracy of 0.4867 versus 0.5333 and Art Style accuracy of 0.6567 versus 0.7233; Table G.1 reports 61.15% generation preference for TexTailor. Most original GenEval and editing point estimates remain unchanged. Changed block selections prevent treating retained or added scores as straightforward same-setting gains between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds an explicit mathematical definition of phrase matching and enhancement-mask construction, including the unmatched-phrase fallback. Appendix G defines custom weighted human-preference scores. The underlying attention and enhancement mathematics remains equivalent, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v1's introduction emphasizes attribute-specialized blocks, particularly later blocks for amount. v2 instead emphasizes similar block behavior across representative attributes and a unified enhancement strategy that generalizes to other attributes. This substantially revises a central finding, while retaining the broad training-free generation, editing, and acceleration claims and headline benchmark gains.

C2.justification: v2 interprets selected blocks as general semantic-processing regions, adds explanations involving stream boundaries, and argues that gains are distinct from CFG upscaling. Appendices B, C.4, and F.5 expand limitations concerning evaluator bias, rare compositions, counting failures, and domain generalization. Acceleration discussion now acknowledges quality-score decreases, replacing v1's unqualified preservation claim with an explicit tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and extensive implementation documentation: Diffusers, precision, checkpoints, per-model inference settings, evaluator prompts, benchmark sampling, token-mask localization, acceleration schedules, and human-study interfaces and scoring. Much of this specifies previously undocumented details rather than demonstrating changed execution. Conflicting acceleration and human-study descriptions limit reproducibility despite the expanded disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of P+, Attend-and-Excite, Semantic Routing, and HyperAlign, plus references supporting new dataset and sampler descriptions. CountGD is removed along with its quantitative probing role. These changes broaden contextual comparisons, while retaining the overarching positioning around systematic block analysis and training-free intervention.

P1.justification: The paper is renamed TexTailor, and the abstract, introduction, and motivation are extensively revised. Related work moves ahead of the analysis, editing and acceleration become a separate Applications section, and a structured appendix documents methods, evaluations, limitations, and examples. These are substantial narrative and organizational changes.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a single-column layout, expands the framework diagram, reorganizes probing plots by model with highlighted selection regions, consolidates the block-selection table, and separates token/full-sentence results. Numerous appendix tables, attention visualizations, failure galleries, and evaluation interfaces are added. Several original qualitative panels are retained and relocated, including v1 Figures 5–6 as v2 Figures 6 and 9.

improvement.justification: The new robustness and transfer tests, failure analysis, and implementation guidance address substantive gaps in v1. However, v2 removes uncertainty summaries and introduces unresolved reporting conflicts: Tables 2 and E.3 disagree on SD3.5 amount scores; acceleration schedules extend beyond the stated 28-step FLUX setting; and three editing participants evaluating 100 samples do not explain Table G.2's 1,200 votes per criterion. These issues affect the auditability of the expanded evidence, preventing a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
